grading.k1: Each series is read on the eve of the release (forward-filled up to seven days for series that skip weekends; the Street consensus is the number posted for that print) and scored against the headline CPI YoY as BLS quotes it (NSA, one decimal). This is the print-eve standard the lead test and the scoreboard use: for the measurements, the Gauge and Truflation on the eve are readings of the month AFTER the one being printed, so this table scores them against a print they are not measuring. It is the test the forecasters face, applied to everyone.
grading.k0: The same-month test, for the measurements only: the calendar-month average of the daily series for the printed month against that print, the like-for-like measurement test. It can only be computed after the month ends, so it is a hindsight comparison, not a forecast.
grading.closest: closest = the series with the smallest absolute error on the eve for that print (ties share it). Rolling MAE = mean absolute error over the last six prints where the series had a reading.
grading.caveat: The CPI Gauge’s daily history is the engine’s publication-dated series (method v1.4 through the day before 2026-09-28, v1.5 from it, the level linked at the switch), not frozen daily vintages; Truflation is the stream as read today; the Cleveland Fed, Street and Kalshi values are the vintages the engine stored on each day. The pre-registered, hashed forecasts live on the scoreboard and in the receipts.

units: percent YoY; errors in percentage points
